correctness.rationale: Central symmetry and the squared-distance identity force the unique center to be zero. Expanding the squared norm of a signed cube corner reduces the radius to minimizing the sum of the positive bond products w_i w_(i+1) among equal-sign neighbors. The sign constraint forces no such bond in even length and permits exactly one in odd length. Strict positivity rules out additional bonds at an optimum. Each maximizing sign pattern is nonconstant and can be uniquely exposed: prescribe nonzero signed cyclic differences with total zero, then integrate to an exposing functional. Strict convexity precludes nonvertex contacts. Cauchy–Schwarz gives precisely the even alternating equality family. For odd length the mean of the single-defect quadratics agrees with the radius squared at uniform weights, and on perturbations the least cyclic-neighbor eigenvalue is -cos(pi/n), giving exactly the stated positive stability coefficient. No optimality is claimed for that coefficient.
residual_risks: Finite replay is corroboration only; the uniform conclusion and stability constant follow from the proof.
